summary: Round-5 verify, everything below MEASURED on the staged tree (each mutant compiled and run with `gradlew :sequencer:test --tests FaultInjectingStoreTest --no-build-cache --rerun`, results dir deleted first so no cached verdict could be reused; unmutated tree = 12 tests / 0 failures; every mutation reverted and the staged diff still hashes e173e623f19e). CLOSED: V2 (row says TWELVE, the file has exactly 12 @Test methods); V3 (the row now says ADR-0029 IS NOT WRITTEN, `decisions/` holds exactly 28 files 0001-0028 and the only ADR-0029 reference in the tree is that line); V4's floor half (M4.20 now owns the faulted-run floor and says so); V6's main half (the row now names duplicatePut-on-putIfMatch as unmodelled); and every item from the parallel test review -- the `unreachable` RECORD is now falsifiable (relabelling get's record to "gone" fails at line 388; stat and list as pure pass-throughs fail), the decorrelation test now covers all three pairs and kills both `seed*3+stream` and aliasing stream 3 onto stream 1, and `List.copyOf` is pinned (returning the live list fails). The new draw-order test IS falsifiable and deterministic: the lazy-draw revert dies at FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:339, and it dies on seed 0 alone -- 25 seeds is far more than enough (unreachable at p=0.05 over 120 calls almost surely fires, so the shift is not a rare event; the reviewer's 200 was generous, not necessary). STILL OPEN: V1 is one third closed. The two putIfMatch mutations V1 named by name both still survive, and so does the same defect on putIfAbsent's duplicate stream -- while the new test's own comment claims those exact mutations as what it pins. No production code changed and no object-store request path is touched: the decorator is test-only, the only request-count effect is the deliberate second conditional PUT of the duplicatePut class, and nothing here scales a request rate with records, shards, partitions or indices.

findings.line: 313-341 (the new test) against FaultInjectingStore.java:218,220 and 150; the overclaim is at FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:318-321
findings.finding: V1 IS ONE THIRD CLOSED, and the test comment claims all of it. V1 named three surviving mutations: the lazy-draw revert and the deletion of either of putIfMatch's two result-discarding draws. MEASURED on the staged tree, each mutant run separately with the test-results directory removed and the build cache off: (a) lazy draws in putIfAbsent -- KILLED, AssertionFailedError at FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:339, and killed even with the loop cut to a single seed; (b) delete `fires(unreachableDraws, faults.unreachable());` at FaultInjectingStore.java:218 -- SURVIVES, 12 tests / 0 failures; (c) delete `fires(duplicateDraws, faults.duplicatePut());` at FaultInjectingStore.java:220 -- SURVIVES, 12 tests / 0 failures. The reason is structural and visible in the new helper: `ambiguousCallsWith` (line 347) drives `putIfAbsent` only, 120 times, and records only the ambiguous stream, so no test in the file ever calls `putIfMatch` more than once -- and the one test that calls it (line 172) runs at ambiguousPut = 1.0, where every draw fires regardless of alignment. A fourth mutation of the same property also survives: move `boolean duplicate = fires(duplicateDraws, ...)` from line 150 to after the unreachable and ambiguous throws (12 tests / 0 failures), because the new test tracks the ambiguous stream and never the duplicate one -- and duplicate is the LAST class drawn, i.e. the one most exposed to being shifted by a class that fires before it. Two claims in the diff are therefore false: FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:318-321 says 'Round-4 review measured three surviving mutations there -- reverting to lazy draws, and deleting either of putIfMatch's two result-discarding draws' as the defect THIS test pins, when it pins one of the three; and the M4.12 row's coverage list (backlog.md:265) says per-class independence is covered 'in BOTH halves ... AND the draw order through the store', when the through-the-store half holds for one verb and one stream. The property is cheap to pin for real: the helper already knows the call index, so interleaving a putIfMatch into the same fixed call sequence and comparing the ambiguous AND duplicate index sets across the unreachable toggle would kill all four.
findings.failure_scenario: FaultInjectingStore.java:218 and 220 are statements whose results are discarded -- exactly what an IDE inspection, a reviewer or a later author calls dead code, and test sources are compiled without -Werror so nothing objects. Delete them (or hoist the three draws into a shared helper that only draws the classes a verb acts on) and the two write verbs stop consuming the same number of draws per call. A simulation run mixes them constantly -- LeaseManager takes putIfMatch, CommitLog takes putIfAbsent -- so from that commit on, toggling one fault class moves the other classes' fault positions again, silently. M4.13's criterion 1 ('each injected fault class must have at least one seed where it changes the outcome') is then reported from a store where per-class attribution is not obtainable, which is the exact defect this file has now shipped a comment about three times, and the suite stays green through all of it. The M4.16 row's seed numbers move for the same reason and the row's 'the seeds have moved twice and the mechanism has not' loses its force, because a moved seed can no longer be distinguished from a broken injector.

findings.finding: The decorrelation test measures a MODEL of the draw, not the draw. MEASURED, both surviving with 12 tests / 0 failures: `fires` rewritten as `return draws.nextFloat() < p;`, and `fires` given an extra `draws.nextDouble();` before the comparison. Neither is caught because the only test of stream independence reimplements the draw in its own helper -- `firesAt` builds `new Random(scramble(seed, stream))` and calls `nextDouble()` once per draw -- so it keeps measuring one-nextDouble-per-decision no matter what the store does. java.util.Random.nextFloat consumes one next(24) where nextDouble consumes next(26)+next(27), so under either mutant the store's actual per-class streams are no longer the streams the test measured, and the 'independent coins' claim covers arithmetic the production path stopped using.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone tightens `fires` -- nextFloat for speed, or a second draw to pick a fault magnitude for M4.13's delayed-write class -- and every test stays green. The independence property is then asserted about a computation nobody runs, and the next time the streams phase-lock it will again be found by measurement rather than by the suite, which is the failure mode this file has already had three times.

findings.finding: The ambiguousPut record's KEY is unpinned, in the one class whose record the file exists to make assertable. MEASURED: replacing `injected.add(new Injected("ambiguousPut", key))` at line 162 with a constant `"?"` leaves 12 tests / 0 failures. The duplicatePut key is pinned (test line 308) and the three read-verb keys are pinned (test line 392); the two ambiguous sites assert kind only. Related, and also unpinned: when ambiguousPut and duplicatePut both fire on one putIfAbsent call, ambiguous throws first and the duplicate is never recorded, so `injected()` systematically under-reports duplicatePut -- V6 raised this and neither the code nor the row says it.
findings.failure_scenario: A sweep reports 'ambiguousPut on ctl/lease/0.json' from a run where the key was fabricated or copied from a neighbouring call, and the debugging session that trusts the record -- which the class javadoc calls the only defence against a silent simulator -- opens the wrong object. The same record is what M4.13 must group by class AND key to satisfy criterion 1.

findings.finding: 'LANDS, THEN REPORTS FAILURE' is not always true, and both the comment and the IOException message state it unconditionally. Both ambiguous branches discard the delegate's result: `delegate.putIfAbsent(...)` at line 161 may return an empty Optional because the key is already taken, and `delegate.putIfMatch(...)` at line 223 may return empty because the version no longer matches. In those cases nothing landed, yet the caller is told 'injected: the write landed but the response was lost' and `injected()` records an ambiguousPut against a key that was never written. The record carries no outcome field, so a reader cannot tell the two apart.
findings.failure_scenario: A seed dies with an I1 or I2 violation and the diagnosis starts from `injected()`. It says ambiguousPut on the slot key, so the analysis assumes the slot exists and the successor lost a race -- when in fact that write lost the CAS cleanly and the real cause is elsewhere. That is exactly the wrong-chain debugging session the read-verb test's own message warns about, arriving through the write side.

findings.finding: Two backlog references still point at rows that do not contain what is handed to them, both non-blocking residue of V4/V5. (1) V5 is unfixed verbatim: M4.20 still reads 'Also `withZone` returns `this`, violating the `Clock` contract -- many logical pods, one seed, through the `Sequencer` seam, with failover both ways ...', splicing the driver's four acceptance criteria onto a defect note as if they elaborated it. (2) M4.20 now says 'the FLOOR half is this row's and the INVARIANT half is M4.16's', and the M4.16 row never mentions `underINJECTEDFaultsTheInvariantsStillHold` or any test at all -- it is the unsealed-ancestor defect plus the ADR-0029 deliverable. M4.16 also asserts in the present tense 'PINNED, not skipped: M4.13's sweep asserts exactly the known-failing seeds and no others', while M4.13 is `todo`, so today nothing pins it.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.20's author reads the row for its criteria, parses the sentence as one clause about withZone, and lands a driver with failover in one direction only -- with nothing in the row to point at. M4.16's author reads its row, finds no invariant assertion, and the one test that would prove the invariants survive injected faults is owned by neither row and is never scheduled; meanwhile a reader takes 'PINNED, not skipped' as a statement about the tree as it stands.
